title: France-French term the OQLF replaces in Quebec
msg: "%s" is the France-French word. Quebec usage (OQLF Grand dictionnaire terminologique) is "%s".

title: English string still sitting in the French file
msg: This value has no French accent and reads as English. A shipped English string in the French build is exactly what an OQLF complaint cites.

title: Euro amount in a Canadian French file
msg: A fr-CA build prices in Canadian dollars. Write the amount as "12,50 $" (comma decimal, dollar sign after the number), not in euros.

title: Slashed day/month/year date
msg: Quebec writes dates as 2026-09-21 (ISO) or "21 septembre 2026". A slashed d/m/y date is read as m/d/y by half your readers.

title: English thousands and decimal separators
msg: French Canadian numbers group with a space and take a comma decimal: 1 234,56 — not 1,234.56.

title: Capital letter stripped of its accent
msg: In Quebec the accent is kept on capitals: "%s" should be "%s".

title: Empty or placeholder translation
msg: This key has no French text. At runtime it falls back to English, and the French build ships an English screen.

title: Locale tag is fr-FR or bare fr
msg: A Quebec build must resolve fr-CA. A bare "fr" or an "fr-FR" tag makes the loader serve France French to Quebec users.

title: Anglicism the OQLF flags
msg: "%s" is an anglicism in this sense. Quebec usage is "%s".
